children: German spot electricity prices rose on Friday, as wind power generation was expected to plunge on Monday from exceptionally high levels.
The German weekend baseload contract (TRDEBWKD1) was up 2% at €141.50 ($164.52) per megawatt-hour by 0748 GMT, LSEG data showed.

German wind power generation is forecast to drop by 24.6 gigawatts to 14.0 GW on Monday, compared with Friday levels, according to LSEG data. German consumption is expected to dip by 0.5 GW to 51.4 GW.
"German wind generation should remain elevated over the weekend before declining on Monday, then recovering later in the week," analysts at Engie's EnergyScan said in a note.
The equivalent French Monday contract (TRFRWKD1) was untraded.

In France, consumption is set to edge up by 0.1 GW to 44.4 GW on Monday. French wind generation is expected to fall by 0.8 GW to 4.4 GW, while solar power output is seen down 0.9 GW to 5.2 GW, according to the data.
Along the curve, the German year-ahead baseload contract (TRDEBYc1) edged down 0.4%.
The equivalent French contract (TRFRBYc1) was untraded.
French nuclear power generation remained at 78% of total capacity.
A total volume of 157.7 terawatt-hours was traded on EPEX SPOT spot and intraday markets in August, up from 128.7 TWh a year earlier, the exchange said in a monthly report.
